title: ADR-0017: Unified Project Hooks
rationale: Two mechanisms for Project entry points (manifest checkables + module functions) is unjustified. One mechanism — Dagger module functions — is simpler, more expressive, and follows the everything-is-Dagger-code paradigm.

title: dagmar-624c: Go port/adapter layer removed — Project Hook Services are Dagger functions
rationale: Env.WithMainModule() registers hook functions natively as LLM tools; conformance via Dagger introspection (Module.Functions()); Tier-B abstraction = Dagger function name, not Go interface. Tracer/Span retained (observability, not a Project Hook Service). dagmar-bootstrap/dagmar-gate untouched (programmatic hooks). os-eco term replaced by Project Hook Services everywhere. Next: dagmar-2cc8 (ADR-0018 code cleanup), then dagmar-c712 (ADR-0019 hook signatures + introspection conformance, blocked by 2cc8).

name: Dagger v0.21.8 LLM Env: Privileged + Writable + Input/Output bindings (cognition proof)
description: EMPIRICALLY PROVEN 2026-08-09: The correct Env setup for dag.LLM().Loop() in v0.21.8 requires EnvOpts{Privileged: true, Writable: true} + WithDirectoryInput('source', dir) + WithDirectoryOutput('result'). Without Privileged, the LLM only sees DeclareOutput + ReadLogs (no file tools). Without Writable, the LLM cannot Save outputs. The workspace via WithWorkspace alone is insufficient — the LLM cannot write files to it. The agent reads from the 'source' input binding, modifies via Directory.withNewFile, and Saves the result to the 'result' output binding. After Loop, read env.Output('result').AsDirectory(). The CLI flag for MaxAPICalls is --max-apicalls (kebab-cased from maxAPICalls, NOT --max-api-calls). Proven via dagger call -m .dagger code --source . --prompt-file <md> --model claude-sonnet-4-20250514 --max-apicalls 15 --module-ref '' — agent successfully read README.md, created COGNITION_PROOF.txt, and saved the result.

SYMPTOM: dag.LLM().Loop() runs but the agent cannot read/write files — it only sees DeclareOutput + ReadLogs tools. CAUSE: Env was created without Privileged:true. Without Privileged, the LLM has no access to the core Dagger API (Directory, File, Container). Additionally, WithWorkspace(dir) alone does NOT provide file write tools — the workspace is read-only context. FIX: use EnvOpts{Privileged:true, Writable:true} + WithDirectoryInput('source', dir) + WithDirectoryOutput('result'). The agent reads from the input, modifies via Directory.withNewFile, and Saves to the output.
resolution: Fixed in code.go: Env now uses Privileged+Writable+Input/Output bindings instead of WithWorkspace. Proven end-to-end.

title: ADR-0022: Env construction for the LLM Loop — Privileged/Writable/IO bindings
rationale: The cognition proof (dagmar-9571) empirically showed that EnvOpts{Privileged:true} is MANDATORY for file tool access; Without it the LLM sees only DeclareOutput+ReadLogs. WithWorkspace alone does not provide write access — must use WithDirectoryInput/Output. ADR-0022 documents the proven pattern + reconciles the Privileged vs hermeticity tension (ADR-0011).

name: ADR-0005 prompt composition runtime: bun+cn in agent pod + jq merge
description: ADR-0005 cross-store composition is delivered at runtime: the agent pod provisions bun (musl build for alpine) + @os-eco/canopy-cli at startup. ShellComposeCommand renders project prompt + DagmarMixins via 'cn render --format json', pipes section objects through jq (reduce .[] as $s ({}; .[$s.name]=$s.body) — last-wins dedup matching Compose() semantics), emits ## section markdown to /tmp/prompt.md. Controller reads Agent.Spec.Prompt.DagmarMixins and passes through agentPodFor -> ensureAgentPod -> Reconcile. Compose() Go function retained as reference implementation. dagmar .canopy/ store created with coder prompt + dagmar-operational mixin.
